entry.name: Alaska Pollock
entry.description: U.S. wild-caught Alaska pollock is managed as several North Pacific stocks. NOAA reports that major assessed stocks are not overfished and the fishery has low incidental catch relative to total catch. Its mild flavor and fine texture make it useful in fillets and surimi.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught, primarily Alaska

entry.name: Pacific Cod
entry.description: Pacific cod is a mild, lean, flaky fish. NOAA describes U.S. wild-caught Pacific cod as sustainably managed under U.S. regulations; harvest methods include longlines and trawls, so origin and gear remain useful buying details.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Source: Look for U.S. wild-caught Pacific cod

entry.name: Haddock
entry.description: Haddock is a mild member of the cod family. NOAA reports that the Georges Bank and Gulf of Maine stocks are not overfished and not subject to overfishing, with management measures addressing habitat and bycatch.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught, New England

entry.name: Tilapia
entry.description: Tilapia has a mild flavor and is widely farmed. FDA/EPA mercury guidance places tilapia in Best Choices, while environmental performance can vary with country, production system, feed, and oversight.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Check the label for origin and farming method.
entry.detail: Source: Farmed; origin and system vary

entry.name: Flounder
entry.description: Flounder is a market name used for several mild flatfish. Mercury guidance groups flounder among Best Choices, but stock status and fishing impacts depend on the exact species, harvest area, and gear.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Ask for the species and origin.
entry.detail: Check label: Species and harvest area matter

entry.name: Catfish
entry.description: Catfish has a mild flavor and firm, moist texture. Products may be U.S.-farmed, imported, or locally caught, so the label and local advisories matter when evaluating a specific fish.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Check local advisories for self-caught catfish.
entry.detail: Check label: Farmed/wild, origin, and species matter

source.sourcetitle: U.S. EPA — Choose Fish and Shellfish Wisely

entry.name: Pacific Whiting
entry.description: Pacific whiting, also called Pacific hake, is a mild West Coast groundfish with soft white flesh. NOAA reports the coastal stock is large and healthy and the U.S. fishery is managed under the Pacific Coast Groundfish plan.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught Pacific whiting

entry.name: Black Sea Bass
entry.description: Black sea bass has a mild, delicate flavor and tender, firm texture. NOAA reports that U.S. stocks are not overfished and that regulations address catch, bycatch, and habitat impacts.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught Atlantic black sea bass

entry.name: Sole
entry.description: Sole is a market name used for several mild, delicate flatfish. FDA/EPA groups sole among Best Choices for mercury, while fishery status and bottom-contact impacts depend on the species, area, and gear.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Ask for the species and origin.
entry.detail: Check label: Species, harvest area, and gear matter

entry.name: Plaice
entry.description: Plaice is a mild flatfish sold fresh or frozen. FDA/EPA lists plaice as a Best Choice for mercury; the name can cover products from different stocks and regions, so origin remains important.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Check label: Species and harvest area matter

entry.name: U.S. Farmed Atlantic Salmon
entry.description: Atlantic salmon sold in U.S. markets is farm-raised. NOAA describes U.S.-farmed Atlantic salmon as regulated by federal, state, and local authorities; imported salmon may be produced under different systems and oversight.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Confirm origin because production standards vary.
entry.detail: Source: This profile applies to U.S.-farmed salmon

entry.name: Atlantic Mackerel
entry.description: Atlantic mackerel is a rich, oily schooling fish. NOAA’s 2025 assessment found the stock not overfished and not subject to overfishing, while noting that it remains under rebuilding management toward its target level.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught Atlantic mackerel

entry.name: Sablefish
entry.description: Sablefish, often marketed as black cod, has a rich, buttery flavor and soft texture. NOAA reports U.S. wild-caught stocks are not overfished and not subject to overfishing.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught, Alaska and West Coast

entry.name: Salmon
entry.description: Salmon can be wild or farmed and can come from several species and regions. FDA/EPA mercury guidance lists salmon as a Best Choice, but sustainability details require the species, origin, and production or harvest method.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Check species and origin.
entry.detail: Check label: Wild/farmed, species, and origin matter

entry.name: Freshwater Trout
entry.description: Freshwater trout includes wild and farmed products from different places. FDA/EPA mercury guidance lists freshwater trout as a Best Choice; local-catch advisories still apply to fish from lakes and rivers.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Check local advisories for self-caught trout.
entry.detail: Source: Wild or farmed; check origin

source.sourcetitle: U.S. EPA — Choose Fish and Shellfish Wisely

entry.name: Bluefish
entry.description: Bluefish has rich, full-flavored meat that is commonly sold fresh or smoked. NOAA reports the Atlantic stock is not overfished but remains under a rebuilding plan toward its target population level.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week. Local advisories may be more restrictive.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught Atlantic bluefish

entry.name: Pacific Chub Mackerel
entry.description: Pacific chub mackerel is an oily schooling fish with a pronounced flavor. NOAA describes U.S. wild-caught Pacific mackerel as managed under the West Coast coastal pelagic species program.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught Pacific mackerel

entry.name: Spanish Mackerel
entry.description: Spanish mackerel is rich, moist, and high in omega-3 fats. NOAA reports the South Atlantic and Gulf stocks are not overfished and not subject to overfishing, with selective fisheries that have low habitat impacts.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught Spanish mackerel

entry.name: Atlantic Striped Bass
entry.description: Atlantic striped bass has firm, flavorful white flesh. NOAA describes the U.S. wild-caught fishery as managed through state and interstate programs; this ocean profile does not replace advisories for landlocked or locally caught striped bass.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice for ocean striped bass; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught Atlantic ocean striped bass

entry.name: Mullet
entry.description: Mullet has moist, flavorful flesh and is sold fresh, smoked, or as roe. FDA/EPA lists mullet as a Best Choice for mercury, while fishery details depend on species and harvest region.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Check label: Species and harvest region matter

entry.name: Atlantic Mahi Mahi
entry.description: Mahi mahi is lean and fairly firm with large, moist flakes. NOAA describes U.S. wild-caught Atlantic mahi mahi as managed under U.S. regulations, while formal stock assessments remain limited in several areas.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught Atlantic mahi mahi

entry.name: Pacific Halibut
entry.description: Pacific halibut has a mild, sweet flavor and firm, flaky texture. NOAA reports the stock is not overfished and fishing occurs at the recommended level under coordinated U.S.-Canada management.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught Pacific halibut

entry.name: Yellowfin Tuna
entry.description: Yellowfin is commonly sold as steaks or used in sushi. FDA/EPA mercury guidance places it in Good Choices; sustainability varies by ocean, stock, and fishing method, so a generic “tuna” label is not enough information.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week.
entry.detail: Check label: Species, ocean, and gear matter

entry.name: Grouper
entry.description: Grouper is a market name for several large reef fish with firm, substantial flakes. Mercury and fishery status differ from one question to the other, and stock conditions vary by species and region.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week. Ask for the exact species and origin.
entry.detail: Check label: Species, region, and fishery matter

entry.name: Albacore Tuna
entry.description: Albacore is sold fresh, frozen, and as canned white tuna. Its mercury category differs from canned light tuna, and fishery performance varies by ocean, stock, and fishing method.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week.
entry.detail: Check label: Albacore species, ocean, and gear matter

entry.name: Rockfish
entry.description: Rockfish is a broad market name, especially for Pacific Sebastes species, with firm fillets and large flakes. Stock status varies by species and harvest area, so a specific label is more useful than the generic name.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week.
entry.detail: Check label: Exact species and harvest area matter

entry.name: Atlantic Tilefish
entry.description: Atlantic tilefish is a firm, mild fish. FDA/EPA treats Atlantic Ocean tilefish as a Good Choice, unlike tilefish from the Gulf of Mexico, which is in the highest-mercury category.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice only when harvested from the Atlantic Ocean; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week.
entry.detail: Origin must say Atlantic Ocean, not Gulf of Mexico

entry.name: Chilean Sea Bass
entry.description: Chilean sea bass is the market name for Patagonian toothfish, a rich fish with large, firm flakes. Fisheries operate under different national and international controls, so origin and traceability are essential buying details.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week.
entry.detail: Check label: Origin and traceability matter

entry.name: Anchovy
entry.description: Anchovies are small schooling fish with a strong savory flavor. FDA/EPA mercury guidance lists anchovy as a Best Choice; stock and harvest information still depends on the fishery.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Check label: Fishery and origin matter

entry.name: Sardine
entry.description: Sardines are small, oily fish sold fresh or canned. FDA/EPA mercury guidance lists sardines as a Best Choice; ask for species and origin when comparing fisheries.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Check label: Species and origin matter

entry.name: Herring
entry.description: Herring are oily schooling fish eaten fresh, smoked, or pickled. FDA/EPA mercury guidance lists herring as a Best Choice; management and bycatch vary among fisheries.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Check label: Fishery and origin matter

entry.name: Smelt
entry.description: Smelt are small fish often cooked whole. FDA/EPA mercury guidance lists smelt as a Best Choice. For self-caught freshwater smelt, consult the advisory for that water body.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Check local advisories for self-caught fish.
entry.detail: Source: Commercial or locally caught

source.sourcetitle: U.S. EPA — Choose Fish and Shellfish Wisely

entry.name: Butterfish
entry.description: Butterfish is a small, schooling Atlantic fish with tender, rich flesh. FDA/EPA lists butterfish as a Best Choice for mercury; fishery conditions and incidental catch controls should be checked by region.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Check label: Fishery and origin matter

entry.name: Shad
entry.description: Shad are oily schooling fish often sold seasonally, while their roe is also marketed separately. FDA/EPA lists shad as a Best Choice for mercury; local rules and advisories still apply to self-caught fish.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Check local advisories for self-caught shad.
entry.detail: Source: Commercial or locally caught; check origin

source.sourcetitle: U.S. EPA — Choose Fish and Shellfish Wisely

entry.name: Atlantic Croaker
entry.description: Atlantic croaker is a relatively small coastal fish with mild white flesh. FDA/EPA lists Atlantic croaker as a Best Choice for mercury; fishery details vary across its Atlantic and Gulf range.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Check label: Harvest region and gear matter

entry.name: White Croaker
entry.description: White croaker, also called Pacific croaker, is a small coastal fish. FDA/EPA places it in Good Choices, and local advisories are especially important because contamination can vary sharply by harvest location.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week. Check local advisories.
entry.detail: Check label: Exact harvest location matters

source.sourcetitle: U.S. EPA — Choose Fish and Shellfish Wisely

entry.name: Pacific Oyster
entry.description: Pacific oysters range from sweet to briny. NOAA describes U.S. farmed and harvested Pacific oysters as regulated under U.S. state and federal requirements; shellfish safety closures and handling guidance remain important.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Follow shellfish safety guidance and cook when advised.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. farmed or harvested Pacific oysters

source.sourcetitle: FDA — Selecting and Serving Seafood Safely

entry.name: Atlantic Sea Scallop
entry.description: Atlantic sea scallops are sweet and firm. NOAA describes the U.S. fishery as sustainably managed; dredge impacts are addressed through rotating access areas, closures, and gear rules.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught Atlantic sea scallop

entry.name: American Lobster
entry.description: American lobster is harvested with traps in the Northwest Atlantic. Management is shared across states and NOAA; current rules also address interactions between vertical lines and protected whales.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught American lobster

entry.name: U.S. Brown Shrimp
entry.description: Brown shrimp is one of the principal shrimp species harvested in the U.S. Southeast. NOAA manages the federal fishery with regional councils, while states manage inshore waters; origin is essential because imported shrimp comes from many systems.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Confirm country and production method.
entry.detail: Source: This profile applies to U.S. wild-caught brown shrimp

entry.name: Clams
entry.description: Clams include many wild and farmed species. FDA/EPA mercury guidance lists clams as a Best Choice. Buy from approved commercial sources because harvest-area closures protect against pathogens and marine toxins.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Follow current shellfish safety advice.
entry.detail: Check label: Species, origin, and harvest approval

source.sourcetitle: FDA — Selecting and Serving Seafood Safely

entry.name: Crab
entry.description: “Crab” covers many species and fisheries. FDA/EPA mercury guidance lists crab as a Best Choice, but source, stock status, trap design, and bycatch differ by species and region.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Ask which crab species and where it was harvested.
entry.detail: Check label: Species and origin matter

entry.name: Longfin Squid
entry.description: Longfin squid has mild, slightly sweet meat and a firm texture. NOAA reports the stock is not overfished, while the current assessment lacks enough information to determine overfishing status.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught Atlantic longfin squid

entry.name: Caribbean Spiny Lobster
entry.description: Caribbean spiny lobster has firm, mildly sweet tail meat and no large front claws. NOAA describes U.S. wild-caught product as managed under U.S. regulations; imported lobster may come from different fisheries.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Source: This profile applies to U.S. wild-caught Caribbean spiny lobster

entry.name: Blue Crab
entry.description: Blue crab is harvested along the Atlantic and Gulf coasts and is especially important in Chesapeake Bay. Populations vary naturally from year to year and are managed primarily by state and interstate programs.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Check label: Harvest region and current local management matter

entry.name: Jonah Crab
entry.description: Jonah crab is a Northwest Atlantic species sold as whole crab, claws, or picked meat. NOAA provides a dedicated U.S. seafood profile; origin and pot-fishery rules remain useful buying context.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for crab during pregnancy, breastfeeding, and childhood.
entry.detail: Source: U.S. wild-caught Northwest Atlantic Jonah crab

entry.name: Carp
entry.description: Carp includes multiple species and can be commercially sold or locally caught. FDA/EPA places carp in Good Choices for mercury; local advisories are especially important for fish taken from inland waters.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week. Check local advisories for self-caught carp.
entry.detail: Source: Commercial or locally caught

source.sourcetitle: U.S. EPA — Choose Fish and Shellfish Wisely

entry.name: Monkfish
entry.description: Monkfish has dense, firm meat. FDA/EPA mercury guidance places it in Good Choices; stock and gear impacts vary, so look for harvest-area information.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week.
entry.detail: Check label: Harvest area and gear matter

entry.name: Skate
entry.description: Skate wing has a distinctive firm texture. FDA/EPA mercury guidance lists skate as a Best Choice; sustainability depends on the skate species, stock, and fishery.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Ask for species and origin.
entry.detail: Check label: Species and stock matter

entry.name: Crawfish
entry.description: Crawfish may be wild-caught or farmed in freshwater systems. FDA/EPA mercury guidance lists crawfish as a Best Choice; production practices and origin still vary.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Check label: Wild/farmed and origin matter

entry.name: Freshwater Perch
entry.description: Freshwater perch includes commercially sold and locally caught fish. FDA/EPA lists freshwater perch as a Best Choice for mercury, but fish from lakes and rivers can carry location-specific contaminant advisories.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Check local advisories for self-caught perch.
entry.detail: Source: Commercial or locally caught; location matters

source.sourcetitle: U.S. EPA — Choose Fish and Shellfish Wisely

entry.name: Ocean Perch
entry.description: Ocean perch is a market name used for marine species that differ from freshwater perch. FDA/EPA lists ocean perch as a Best Choice for mercury; exact species and fishery should still be identified.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children.
entry.detail: Check label: Exact species and harvest area matter

entry.name: Pickerel
entry.description: Pickerel is a freshwater fish that may be sold commercially or caught locally. FDA/EPA lists pickerel as a Best Choice for mercury, but waterbody-specific advisories take priority for self-caught fish.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Check local advisories for self-caught pickerel.
entry.detail: Source: Commercial or locally caught; location matters

source.sourcetitle: U.S. EPA — Choose Fish and Shellfish Wisely

entry.name: Whitefish
entry.description: Whitefish can refer to freshwater lake whitefish or to a broad retail grouping. FDA/EPA lists whitefish as a Best Choice for mercury, while stock and local-contaminant details depend on species and origin.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Best Choice for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children. Check local advisories for self-caught fish.
entry.detail: Check label: Exact species and origin matter

source.sourcetitle: U.S. EPA — Choose Fish and Shellfish Wisely

entry.name: Buffalofish
entry.description: Buffalofish are native North American freshwater fish and are distinct from invasive Asian carp. FDA/EPA places buffalofish in Good Choices; local advisories remain important for fish caught from inland waters.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Good Choice; during pregnancy or breastfeeding, choose one serving that week. Check local advisories.
entry.detail: Source: Commercial or locally caught; location matters

source.sourcetitle: U.S. EPA — Choose Fish and Shellfish Wisely

entry.name: King Mackerel
entry.description: King mackerel is one of seven fish in FDA/EPA’s highest-mercury category. This health classification is separate from fishery status: a fishery can be managed while the species still carries consumption advice for sensitive groups.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Choice to Avoid for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children because of the highest mercury levels.
entry.detail: Health guidance: Highest-mercury category

entry.name: Marlin
entry.description: FDA/EPA places marlin in its highest-mercury category. Different marlin species and fisheries have separate conservation concerns, so health and sustainability questions should be evaluated independently.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Choice to Avoid for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children because of the highest mercury levels.
entry.detail: Health guidance: Highest-mercury category

entry.name: Orange Roughy
entry.description: Orange roughy is a long-lived deep-water fish. FDA/EPA places it in its highest-mercury category; origin-specific stock and habitat impacts should also be checked.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Choice to Avoid for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children because of the highest mercury levels.
entry.detail: Health guidance: Highest-mercury category

entry.name: Shark
entry.description: “Shark” covers many species with very different conservation status, but FDA/EPA groups shark in its highest-mercury category. Ask for the exact species; many shark populations also face slow reproduction and fishing pressure.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Choice to Avoid for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children because of the highest mercury levels.
entry.detail: Health guidance: Highest-mercury category

entry.name: Swordfish
entry.description: Swordfish is a large, long-lived predator commonly sold as firm steaks. FDA/EPA places swordfish in its highest-mercury category.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Choice to Avoid for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children because of the highest mercury levels.
entry.detail: Health guidance: Highest-mercury category

entry.name: Gulf of Mexico Tilefish
entry.description: FDA/EPA distinguishes tilefish by harvest area: tilefish from the Gulf of Mexico is in the highest-mercury category, while Atlantic Ocean tilefish appears in Good Choices. The location on the label changes the guidance.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Choice to Avoid for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children when the tilefish is from the Gulf of Mexico.
entry.detail: Origin: Gulf of Mexico only

entry.name: Bigeye Tuna
entry.description: Bigeye is one tuna species and should not be confused with canned light tuna or yellowfin. FDA/EPA places bigeye tuna in its highest-mercury category.
entry.advice: FDA/EPA mercury guidance: Choice to Avoid for pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children because of the highest mercury levels.
entry.detail: Species: Bigeye tuna specifically
